site.title: The Model Map
site.description: Twenty-five AI models from thirteen vendors, priced and labeled. Compare cost, context, licensing and capability, then work out what your own setup would cost.
site.lede: Twenty-five models from thirteen vendors, priced and labeled. No single model wins everything, and the right pick is usually decided by budget and constraints before it's decided by benchmark. Read down for the shape of the market, or jump to the end to work out your own setup.

board.heading: The top of the board
board.note: Scores are the Artificial Analysis composite index, which measures intelligence rather than value. Gemini 3 Pro (Google) leads multimodal work rather than the composite. Grok 4.5 (xAI) is the cheapest model in the top 10 at $2 per million output tokens. And the open-weight field sits close behind the podium: GLM-5.2 beats GPT-5.5 on SWE-bench Pro. The podium is real, but most working decisions happen below it.

tiers.name: Frontier
tiers.models: Claude Fable 5 / Opus 5 · GPT-5.6 Sol · Gemini 3 Pro · Grok 4.5
tiers.buy: Deep reasoning, long-running agents, the hardest problems. Correctness matters more than cost here, which makes it a tier for funded work rather than routine volume. Grok 4.5 is the budget door in.

tiers.name: Workhorse
tiers.models: Claude Sonnet 5 · GPT-5.6 standard · Gemini 3.5 Flash · Grok 4.5 · Perplexity Sonar Pro · Nemotron 3 Ultra
tiers.buy: Roughly 85 to 95 percent of frontier quality at a third the price or less. The sane default for production work across every vendor. Perplexity's Sonar models sit here with a twist: live web search and citations are bundled into the token price, so they answer from the current web rather than from memory.

tiers.name: Small / fast
tiers.models: Qwen 3.7 Flash · DeepSeek V4-Flash · Nemotron 3 Nano · Nemotron 3 Super · Claude Haiku 4.5 · Gemini Flash-Lite
tiers.buy: Sorting, tagging, extracting, routing. Anything where volume is the whole problem and a large model is wasted money.

tiers.name: Open-weight
tiers.models: GLM-5.2 · DeepSeek V4 Pro · Qwen 3 235B · MiniMax M3 · Kimi K2.6 · Mistral Large 3 · Llama 4 · Nemotron 3 (NVIDIA)
tiers.buy: Models you can download and run yourself. The fastest-moving part of the market, and where most real volume goes. Each of these has a genuine specialty rather than being a cheap copy of a frontier model.

tiers.name: Specialist
tiers.models: Image and video generation · embeddings · computer-use models
tiers.buy: A different axis entirely. Ranked per task rather than on intelligence indexes, and out of scope for this map.

routing.title: Prototype on a frontier model
routing.body: Get the task working where capability is not the bottleneck, so you learn what the job actually requires before you optimize.

routing.title: Move volume to a cheap tier
routing.body: Re-run the same prompts on a small or open model and compare the results. Most production work holds up, and the bill drops by an order of magnitude.

routing.title: Escalate only what earns it
routing.body: Send the requests that measurably fail on the cheap model back to the expensive one. That subset is usually far smaller than expected.

routing.title: Cache aggressively
routing.body: Caching repeated context and using batch pricing cuts large-model costs substantially. It changes the absolute numbers, never the ordering.

retentionCallout.label: If your company forbids data retention
paras: Some frontier models require the vendor to keep your data for a period and are unavailable to companies that forbid it. Claude Fable 5 is one. Open-weight models sidestep the question entirely when you host them yourself. The tool below has a filter for this.
One caveat on that filter: Fable 5 is the only model here confirmed to require retention, so the others pass by default. Confirm the current terms with any vendor before you rely on it contractually.
